label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, B, D where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (a rusted 55-gallon drum, upright, with a hazard stripe), every view shows a plain upright cylinder with a flat lid and a flat base, the same outline from the front, back, left, right and both three-quarter views. The top view is faceted (about 14 sides) but reads as round at this scale, and no part sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Measured 23.4 x 23.4 x 36 against the brief's 23 across and 34 high: across is 1.8% off, height 5.9% off, inside the 15% band.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, checked down to the small ones: drum body, flat lid, flat base, the bung on the lid (visible in the top, front-left and back-left views), the top and bottom rolling bands (front, left, back and right views), and the hazard stripe at mid-height (all four side views). None is missing. The bung sits at the lid's centre rather than near the rim, which is a placement choice the brief does not fix.

M4.reason: Body is a blue-grey painted steel, the bands are rust-brown and the stripe is yellow with black, each region reads as the material the brief names. Within the same colour family at this scale.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe is sharp, diagonal, in place and at a sensible sharpness. The brief's rust is on the two bands and the lid rim only; the drum body, in every side view, is clean blue-grey with faint mottling and almost no rust or wear, so the 'rusted' surface the brief asks for is thin on the body (front, left, back, right views).

M6.reason: Capped at 2 for this model by the rubric's line-up test. In the four-way line-up the asset was picked as not made by Valve in no reading (it was at D, A, C, C in the four orders and judges picked C, D, B, D), so it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: Upright, lid up, bung on top, base flat on the ground plane in the front and oblique views. A drum has no front to mark, so the stripe's orientation is the only facing and it runs level all round.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. 224 triangles is under the 422 that Half-Life spends at most on its props of this kind and size (median 99, three quarters under 156, so this is above the kit's warning line but well under the most Valve spends). Nothing is open to the eye: the lid has its bung, the base is closed (below view), and nothing floats or is inside out.
